title: Ecuadorian priest dies after giant cross falls on him during livestreamed Mass
desc: Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari died on Saturday, October 17, after a large wooden crucifix fell on him during Mass in Guayaquil. The incident was captured during a live broadcast, while the Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed his death and expressed condolences. An Ecuadorian Catholic priest died after a large wooden cross detached from a church wall and struck him while he was celebrating Mass in the city of Guayaquil, according to local media reports. The priest, identified as Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari, was leading the service at the Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church when the crucifix fell from the wall behind him on Saturday, October 17. The Mass was being broadcast live on social media when the incident occurred, with footage showing the large crucifix falling onto the priest near the 27th minute of the service. Worshippers rushed to help following the impact, while cries of alarm could be heard in the recording. The footage subsequently circulated online, drawing widespread attention to the fatal accident. The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed Sánchez Molinari's death in an official statement, identifying him as the parish priest of the church in the archdiocese's Central Vicariate. The archdiocese expressed its condolences to the Redemptorist religious community, the priest's relatives and his friends, and called for prayers for the repose of his soul. Sánchez Molinari was a member of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Catholic religious order also known as the Redemptorists. As of October 18, the cause of the cross's detachment had not been officially established. The archdiocese's statement confirmed the priest's death but did not provide further details about the circumstances of the accident.

title: A transformer-enhanced U-Net with FiLM-driven clinical conditioning for multi-task breast ultrasound lesion analysis
desc: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection of breast lesions using non-invasive imaging techniques is crucial for improving timely diagnosis, treatment outcomes, and patient prognosis. This study aims to develop and evaluate hybrid deep learning models for breast-lesion segmentation and classification in ultrasound images using patient-level cross-validation. Challenges such as low contrast, imaging artifacts, and irregular lesion morphology can limit accurate diagnosis, highlighting the need for advanced deep learning approaches for reliable breast-lesion analysis. Recent developments in deep learning, particularly hybrid architectures that combine convolutional and transformer representations, have shown promise in addressing these constraints. We present three Hybrid Deep Learning (HDL) models. Three complementary deep learning models were evaluated for breast lesion classification and segmentation using the Breast-Lesions-USG dataset. Model 1 employed DoubleHeadUNet with a ResNet-34 backbone, Model 2 combined a Swin V2 Transformer with a U-Net decoder, and Model 3 integrated a Hybrid Transformer-FiLM U-Net to incorporate clinical metadata. Patient-level five-fold cross-validation with strict patient separation and nested hyperparameter selection was employed. Model 1 achieved the highest accuracy (82.94%) and AUC (87.70%), while Model 3 demonstrated the highest malignant recall (81.63%) and strongest segmentation performance (Dice: 0.901; IoU: 0.825). Model 2 achieved an accuracy of 79.76% and an AUC of 87.54%. Statistical analysis indicated that most accuracy differences were not significant, supporting the complementary strengths of the three models rather than identifying a universally superior approach. Comparisons with previous studies were considered indicative due to differences in datasets and evaluation protocols.
